subject: Climate & Environment
title: The End of Coal
description: Learn The End of Coal in one minute.

hook.text: Coal powered the Industrial Revolution. Now it is being retired faster than anyone expected.

buildup.text: Burning coal produces twice the CO₂ of natural gas for the same energy output.

discovery.text: New solar and wind are now cheaper than running existing coal plants in most of the world.

twist.text: China still builds new coal plants — while also installing more renewables than any nation.

climax.text: Coal employment has fallen 60% globally since 2015. The transition reshapes entire communities.

punchline.text: Coal isn't dying from regulation. It's dying from math.

quiz.question: Why is coal losing to renewables economically?
options: New solar and wind are cheaper than existing coal

details.summary: Coal is the most carbon-intensive fossil fuel and the single largest source of energy-related CO2 emissions. Globally, coal use is declining in developed countries as renewables become cheaper, but consumption continues to grow in parts of Asia, where hundreds of new plants are still being built.
details.whyItMatters: Phasing out coal is the single most impactful climate action. Yet coal still generates about 35 percent of global electricity, and closing plants involves complex economic and political challenges.
takeaways: Coal is the largest source of CO2 from electricity generation
Developed nations are closing coal plants as renewables grow
New coal plants are still being built across parts of Asia

faq.question: When will the last coal plant close?
faq.answer: Many developed countries target coal exit by 2030 to 2035. However, China and India, which rely heavily on coal, have not committed to firm timelines. Global coal use may not peak until the late 2020s, with full phase-out potentially taking decades longer.

faq.question: What happens to coal workers when plants close?
faq.answer: Just transition programs aim to retrain workers, invest in affected communities, and create alternative employment. Success varies widely. Without adequate support, coal closures can devastate local economies that have depended on mining for generations.
